faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.answer:

If there are gaps in the nozzle check pattern, clean the print head nozzles.
If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.question: Are there different size ink cartridges available?
faqs.answer: The printer only supports one ink size; 700 ml per color, 600 ml for white, and 350 ml for silver.

faqs.question: What is in the Ink Starter Pack?
faqs.answer: The pack includes one cartridge of each color and a full set of cleaning cartridges specific to the color configuration of your printer (CMYK, CMYKW, etc.).

faqs.question: How long does an ink circulation take?
faqs.answer: It takes about 10-15 minutes. We recommend that you do a manual circulation at the beginning of each day to prevent the printer from doing an ink circulation while you print.

faqs.question: Can I use 3rd party ink?
faqs.answer: In order to ensure printer reliability, color consistency, and image quality, we recommend that you use only Epson genuine inks.

faqs.question: Can I turn off the white and silver ink if I decide I no longer want to use it?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You'll need to have an Epson technician perform this task.
Note:
Once it's done, it cannot be reversed.

faqs.question: Can I add white and silver ink if I decide I want to use it later?
faqs.answer: No. Once the printer is installed without the white and silver ink, the ink configuration is permanent.

faqs.question: Are the white and silver ink cartridges included with my product?
faqs.answer: No, they are optional.

faqs.question: How can I give the ink more time to dry before it goes through the take-up reel?
faqs.answer:
Press the printer's
Menu
button, select
Media Setup
>
Customize Settings
, then select your media. Select
Heater & Drying
>
Dry Time Per Pass,
then increase the time so the print head will pause a fixed amount of time between passes.

faqs.question: How long will the cartridges last in the box?
faqs.answer: The cartridges are good for 2 years from the manufactured date when the box is sealed. After you open the cartridges, they should be used within 6 months to assure optimal quality.

faqs.question: Is there any nickel in the yellow ink?
faqs.answer: No. The UltraChrome GS2 and UltraChrome GSX inks contain no nickel.

faqs.question: I can't shake the white or silver ink cartridges for a week. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
We recommend that you perform pre-storage maintenance. See
Notes when not using the printer
for more information.

faqs.question: Which ink cartridges are included with my product?
faqs.answer: The ink cartridges are not included. You'll need to purchase the Ink Starter Pack (part number GS2INK4H). The pack includes a full set of ink cartridges and cleaning cartridges. The number of cartridges included will depend on your printer's color configuration. The printer is designed to be used exclusively with specially-formulated Epson inks, and not with other brands of cartridges or ink.

faqs.question: Can I use the same ink cartridges in all Epson SureColor products?
faqs.answer: No. The S30670 and the S50670 use the same ink cartridges, while the S70670 uses a different set of ink cartridges. The S50670 and S70670 use the same white ink cartridges.

faqs.question: When should I use the manual feed adjustment?
faqs.answer: You should only do the adjustment when an automatic media feed adjustment fails or print quality is not acceptable.

faqs.question: What benefit does the optional dryer (standard on S50670) provide?
faqs.answer: It will ensure that your prints are dry by the time they reach the end of the post heater.

faqs.question: How do I perform a media feed adjustment while printing is in progress?
faqs.answer: Press the printer's up or down buttons (media feed buttons) while you print; you'll be able to adjust the feed by 5%. This is useful if you see banding on a print. However, it may introduce registration issues.

faqs.question: When should I perform a head washing or single channel washing?
faqs.answer: Perform the process only if you have nozzles that are unrecoverable after many cleanings and manual head maintenance. The process should be your last resort; it will require cleaning cartridges and uses a significant amount of ink.

faqs.question: When should I replace the wipers, flushing pads, and wiper cleaners included in my maintenance kit?
faqs.answer: It will depend on how much you use your printer; replace them every 3-6 months.

faqs.question: How much cleaning fluid do the cleaning cartridges use during initialization?
faqs.answer: Approximately 100 ml.

faqs.question: What comes in the Epson maintenance kit?
faqs.answer:
It includes the following:
Gloves x2
Instruction manual
Large cleaning sticks
Replacement flushing pads x2
Replacement wipers x2
Replacement wiper cleaners x2
T-Wiper

faqs.question: When should I perform a light, medium, or heavy cleaning?
faqs.answer:
It depends on the results of your nozzle check. Perform a light cleaning when only a few nozzles are clogged, a medium cleaning when multiple nozzles are clogged, and a heavy cleaning when a whole channel is out.
See
Head cleaning
in the User's Guide for more information.

faqs.question: How do I perform a cleaning during a print job?
faqs.answer:
Press the printer's
button (maintenance button). The printer will pause and do a cleaning.
Note:
If the printer pauses a few seconds during a print job, a print quality issue may occur; the issue will depend on the media you use.

faqs.question: How should I clean ink off of the rollers?
faqs.answer: Generously soak a large cleaning stick in ink cleaning solution, then clean the affected rollers by vigorously rubbing around the top and bottom.

faqs.question: Can I perform an ink circulation manually?
faqs.answer: Yes. The white and silver inks can be performed manually. The option is on the printer's control panel.

faqs.question: Should I use the 100 mm, 200 mm, or 500 mm manual feed adjustment?
faqs.answer: We recommend that you always use the 500 mm manual feed adjustment; the longer pattern is more effective.

faqs.question: What should I do with the waste ink?
faqs.answer: Check your local regulations and contact a local disposal service if needed.

faqs.question: How often does the ink circulate?
faqs.answer: Once every 24 hours. Only the S50670 and S70670 with white and silver ink installed will do an ink circulation routine. The ink system on the printer utilizes an ink recirculation system for the white and silver colors; this process considerably reduces the amount of ink used to maintain the ink system.

faqs.question: How much cleaning fluid do the cleaning cartridges use during cleaning?
faqs.answer: Approximately 125 ml. You should be able to use the cleaning cartridges multiple times.

faqs.question: Where can I find the ink Safety Data Sheet (SDS)?
faqs.answer: See the Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for your product.

faqs.question: How often should I shake the cartridges?
faqs.answer: It is required that you shake the white and silver cartridges once a day; the printer's control panel will notify you. We recommend that you shake all other cartridges at least once a week to ensure color consistency.

faqs.question: What are the ruler-like marks on the heater and the rear of my product?
faqs.answer: They are visual guides that'll help you identify if the media is not properly aligned or if it's skewed when it feeds through the printer.

faqs.question: How often should I perform maintenance and at what level?
faqs.answer: The frequency will depend on how much you use the printer. For regular use, we recommend that you perform maintenance once a week. For heavy use, we recommend maintenance every 2-3 days, and for extreme use we recommend once a day.

faqs.question: How do I clean the media edge guides?
faqs.answer: Remove the media edge guides from the printer, soak a large cleaning stick in ink cleaning solution, then vigorously clean the built-up ink on the media edge guides. If the media edge guides are damaged or bent, you can order replacements (part number C890891).

faqs.question: How long should I wait before I laminate a print?
faqs.answer: Wait at least 24 hours after you print; this will allow the print to cure.

faqs.question: What is the thickest media my product will feed?
faqs.answer: 1 millimeter.

faqs.question: Do I need to off-gas and/or cure a print before I laminate it?
faqs.answer: Yes, 24 hours of off-gas time is recommended before you laminate your prints.

faqs.question: Do I need to align the take-in and take-up reels?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need to align the reels to avoid registration, banding, and paper feed issues. You'll only need to do this once during setup, unless the printer is moved or the system becomes misaligned. We recommend that you keep the alignment paper for future use.

faqs.question: My product came with stickers with three black bars on them. Where should I put them?
faqs.answer: The stickers should line up with the three roller spaces closest to the control panel. They serve as a guide when you load media from the back of the printer.

faqs.question: How do I turn off the alert buzzer?
faqs.answer:
Press the printer's
Menu
button, select
Preference
>
Alert Sound Settings
>
Off
.

faqs.question: Do I need to perform a separate feed adjustment when I use the green rollers?
faqs.answer: Yes, a 500mm feed adjustment is necessary. We recommended that you create a separate custom media setting when you use the green rollers.

faqs.question: Does GamaPrint Pro support white/silver ink?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it's limited. If you plan to use white and silver ink for production applications, we strongly recommend you upgrade to Postershop or Production House.

faqs.question: What upgrades are available for my ONYX RIP?
faqs.answer: Check with your local ONYX authorized reseller; upgrades are available from an authorized reseller.

faqs.question: Do I need to ventilate my product?
faqs.answer: No. Special ventilation is not required with one printer in an adequately sized room with sufficient natural airflow. However, if you have more than one printer, check your local regulations.

faqs.question: My product automatically prints jobs after they're ripped. How do I stop this?
faqs.answer:
Open
Rip Queue,
right-click on the printer, select
Modify Printer
>
Setup,
then uncheck
Automatically Start Printing.
Click
OK
.

faqs.question: Where can I tell my product that the media is printable side in?
faqs.answer: The custom media setup process has an option to set the roll type to printable side in or printable side out, or you can set it during the media loading process.

faqs.question: The ONYX software shows that my product is not connected. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure your printer is connected to your computer. If the connection is fine, try the following:
Click
Configure Printer
.
Select the
Device
tab >
Configure Port
>
TCP/IP
>
Configure
.
Verify that the IP address in the software matches the IP address on your printer. To see your printer's IP address, select
Menu
>
Printer Settings
>
Network Settings
>
IP
.
Click
Test
to verify the connection.

faqs.question: Does the additional dryer require an additional power outlet?
faqs.answer: Yes, it requires one additional 110v outlet and 45w of power (3 amps).

faqs.question: Do I need to level my product?
faqs.answer: Yes, the printer should be placed on a level surface.

faqs.question: How do I set a static IP address on my product?
faqs.answer:
You can set it with the EpsonNet Config Utility (recommended) or the printer's control panel. It's easier to set it with the utility. You can install the utility from the printer's CD or from the Downloads tab for your product. After you install the utility, follow the instructions in the
EpsonNet Config Operations Guide
to configure your printer. The guide will be installed on your computer when you install the utility.

faqs.question: What temperature do you recommend for the heater and how do I set it?
faqs.answer:
The temperature you set will depend on the media you use; see your media's documentation for recommendations.
You can set the temperature during the custom media setup (recommended) or on the printer's control panel.
See
Changing Heater and Fan Settings
in the printer's User's Guide for detailed information.

faqs.question: Should I adjust the manual feed by millimeters or inches?
faqs.answer:
We recommend that you use millimeters. This will ensure that you get the best possible adjustment and will also minimize banding.
Note:
Later firmware releases will only support millimeters.

faqs.question: When should I use multi-layer printing?
faqs.answer: Multi-layer printing is used in certain cases with spot colors, particularly if a base layer of white or silver is required. When printing more than full color and one spot color at the same time, or when the dry time of a base layer is required, multi-layer printing is effective.

faqs.question: Which profiles are included with the software?
faqs.answer: Epson provides about 100 profiles for your printer; they're included with GamaPrint Pro and are available for download for Postershop and Production House. They support 3M, Avery, Neschen, Ultraflex, and Epson media in various configurations and models.

faqs.question: Does GamaPrint Pro include profiling capabilities?
faqs.answer: No. You must upgrade your version of ONYX RIP. Contact an authorized reseller for information on how to upgrade.

faqs.question: Are other RIPs available?
faqs.answer: Yes, the printer is compatible with most 3rd party RIPs.

faqs.question: Why should I create a custom media type?
faqs.answer: It will ensure that the printer produces optimal print quality. Using this setup will maximize the printer's capabilities.

faqs.question: Should I use the Accuphoto or Stochastic profile?
faqs.answer: Epson recommends Accuphoto for the best print quality.

faqs.question: How do I test my IP connection?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:

Configure Printer
.
Select the
Device
tab >
Configure Port
>
TCP/IP
>
Configure
.
Verify that the IP address in the software matches the IP address on your printer. To see your printer's IP address, select
Menu
>

>
Network Settings
>
IP
.
Click

to verify the connection.

faqs.question: Do I need to RIP a job again if I want to print it again?
faqs.answer: No. You can print it again by dragging the past job onto the print queue.

faqs.question: When should I use the green rollers?
faqs.answer: Use them when you perform printing with specialty inks. When the green rollers are engaged, your print will not be marred when it rolls back (in preparation) for multiple layer printing.

faqs.question: What do I need to set up my product?
faqs.answer:
You will need the following:
500 mm ruler
2 furniture dollies (optional)
5 people (for placing the printer on stand)
Ample space
Identified power source
Knife/scissors for opening packaging
Pen/pencil
Windows based computer (for drivers and the ONYX RIP)

faqs.question: Can I save a job in Layout Tool?
faqs.answer: Yes. We recommend that you save the job so you don't need to layout the job again. This is helpful if you've made edits such as color correction, sizing, etc.

faqs.question: When should I use the rubber weights?
faqs.answer: Use them when you print on heavy banner or thin/difficult media. They will keep the tension on the take-up reel even. We recommend that you load them evenly on the tension bar of the take-up reel and use 3 on each side (not 1 or 2).

faqs.question: What features are included with my version of ONYX RIP?
faqs.answer: The standard version of GamaPrint Pro includes Layout Tool, Rip-Queue, Color Correction, and the ability to print to one printer. If you have a five color printer, the RIP will support printing with spot (white/metallic silver) colors.

faqs.question: Where can I select the direction of the take-up reel?
faqs.answer: There is a switch on the take-up reel roll holder closest to the printer's control panel. You can set it to automatic direction or manual control.

faqs.question: Rip-Queue indicates printing is in progress by displaying a percent status, but then it drops the print job, and nothing prints (with an Ethernet connection). What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure your network cables are properly connected. If the connection is fine, try the following:
Make sure the IP address is the same in Rip-Queue and on the printer.
Click
Configure Printer
.
Select the
Device
tab >
Configure Port
>
TCP/IP
>
Configure
.
Verify that the IP address in the software matches the IP address on your printer. To see your printer's IP address, select
Menu
>
Printer Settings
>
Network Settings
>
IP
.
If you are printing to the Windows COM driver, make sure you have the correct profile assigned in the COM driver.
Note:
The entire job must spool before printing begins.

faqs.question: How can I verify that I'm using the latest firmware on my product?
faqs.answer:
Determine your printer's firmware version, then go to the Downloads tab for your product and compare the latest version to the one on your printer.
To see your printer's firmware version, press the
Menu
button, select
Printer Status
, then
Firmware Version
on the printer
.
Use
LFP Remote Panel
(do not use the automatic acquire feature) to update the firmware.

faqs.question: How do I share custom media types?
faqs.answer:
In LFP Remote Panel, back up and save (to a file) your custom media settings, then share the file with other printers.
Note:
Media feed and head alignments are not stored in the file. They must be done on each printer and for each media type you use.

faqs.question: Does the RIP support cutting?
faqs.answer: GamaPrint Pro requires an upgrade for cutting support ($495). Postershop and Production House include cutting support.

faqs.question: How long will it take to set up my product?
faqs.answer: The printer assembly will take approximately one hour and will require five people to attach the printer to the printer stand. The printer initialization, alignment, and software installation will take an additional two hours.

faqs.question: Which interfaces does my product support?
faqs.answer: Gigabit Ethernet and USB 2.0. Both interfaces can be connected at the same time; the printer will automatically switch between them.

faqs.question: How do I save my Epson printer driver presets so I can restore them if I reinstall the Epson printer driver in Windows?
faqs.answer:
Note:
You may lose some custom settings when you uninstall the printer driver.
Before you reinstall the printer driver, do the following:
Open
File Explorer
or
Windows Explorer
.
Select
This PC
or
Computer
>
C:
drive >
Program Files
>
Epson
> [your printer name].
Move the UCI extension files to a different folder on your desktop.
Note:
After you reinstall the Epson printer driver, move the UCI extension files back to your printer's folder as described in step 2.

faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Download the ICC profiles for your printer and save them in a folder you can easily find.
Close all open software.
Open
Windows Explorer
, then select
Computer
>
C:
drive >
Windows
>
System32
>
spool
>
drivers
>
color
.
Move the ICC profiles into the
color
folder, then close all open windows.

faqs.answer:
See our
Installing a Printer in Windows 11 24H2 or Later

faqs.question: What comes with the HD substrate support system?
faqs.answer: It includes a new matched take-in reel and take-up reel.

faqs.question: How long can I leave my product off?
faqs.answer:
We recommend that you leave the printer on all the time; this will allow the printer to perform required automatic cleanings. If you'll be away from the printer for more than a week, and white/silver ink is installed, we recommend that you perform an Ink Refresh to avoid possible nozzle clogs. See the
Refresh
section in the User's Guide for more information.

faqs.question: What are the limits on the standard substrate support system?
faqs.answer: It supports rolls up to 90 lbs.

faqs.question: How much power does my product consume?
faqs.answer: Approximately 895 W while operating and 775 W in standby mode with the heater on and 30 W with the heater off.

faqs.question: What comes in my product box?
faqs.answer:
The following are included:
Alignment sheet
S-Series printer
Dryer
Extra maintenance kit
Electronic instruction manual
ONYX GamaPrint Pro
Power cables
Communication Driver
Printer stand
Sample media
Substrate support system
Note:
The Ink Starter Pack must be purchased separately.

faqs.question: Can I extend my current service plan?
faqs.answer: You can extend the plan as long as your printer is currently covered. Plans can be extended at any time.

faqs.question: Why should I use the HD (heavy duty) substrate support system?
faqs.answer: It is optimal for environments that use print rolls heavier than 90 lbs.

faqs.question: Who do I contact for support?
faqs.answer: You can call Epson support at (888)-377-6611. Please have your unit ID and serial number ready when you call.

faqs.question: What is the minimum door width my product will fit through?
faqs.answer: 50 inches. This is due to the width of the heater.

faqs.question: When would I need the additional dryer?
faqs.answer: If you run high speed production jobs, the additional dryer will shorten the dry time and improve print quality. The optional dryer is also useful when you use white or silver ink.

faqs.question: What extended service plans are available?
faqs.answer:
Each printer is covered for one year. For more information on the terms of this plan, go to
proimaging.epson.com
, select your printer, then select the Options tab. Click
Terms and Conditions
.

faqs.question: What is the maximum printable width my product can print?
faqs.answer:
63.60".
Note:
The printer is not capable of borderless printing.

faqs.question: Do my products have VOCs?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they do not require any special ventilation or air purification.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the PE and the HD (heavy duty) version?
faqs.answer: The HD version includes a HD substrate support system which handles media rolls up to 175 lbs. The PE version includes a standard substrate support system which handles media rolls up to 90 lbs. Both systems include take-in and take-up reels.

faqs.answer:
See our
